analysis.title: Bond Turbulence: Q&A with Dominic Nolan (October 2026 Q&A)
key_insights: September was a poor month for bonds. The 10-year Treasury yield rose from 4.8% to more than 5.2% and the Bloomberg US Aggregate Bond Index returned -2.6%. The S&P 500 was slightly negative, with growth stocks positive.

The author attributes the yield rise to elevated inflation, persistently high energy prices, fading hopes for a resolution of the Iran conflict, and developments in the Russia-Ukraine war. The Fed raised the federal funds rate to 3.75%-4% at its September meeting.
The AI and data center buildout is described as arguably the largest infrastructure build in US history. It adds to inflationary pressure and to hundreds of billions of dollars in bond issuance.

Meta returned nearly 27% in September after the September 8 launch of its consumer AI agent Muse, which the author says helps justify Meta's $130-145B 2026 capex. Broadcom was the Mag 7 + Broadcom laggard at -5%.
Nvidia raised its buyback authorization by $150B, a US record, to a total of $235B. The stock rose about 3.6% in September and its market cap is approaching $6T.

The US economy shows resilience. Q2 real GDP was revised up from 1.5% to 2.2%, nominal GDP grew 8.5%, and the Atlanta Fed GDPNow for Q3 has been around 3.6%. Energy and gas prices rose at double-digit rates in August.

The labor market is softer. September payrolls were +29,000 against 84,000 expected, unemployment rose to 4.2%, and July and August were revised down by a combined 60,000. Stocks rallied on the release because it eased pressure on the Fed to hike.

Wages rose 3% y/y, below inflation. Bank of America card data show spending up more than 6% y/y for the four weeks to September 26, which the author reads as consumers drawing on savings. Gas spending rose nearly 23% and airlines 12.8%.

The author argues the AI build and high energy prices offset each other. With stable energy, asset prices would be higher, and without the AI build, growth would be slower and asset prices lower. The average worker is being strained.

The bond selloff is global. 10-year yields are up roughly 300-450 bps since 2021 in the US, UK, France, Germany and Japan. Japan's 10-year is up nearly 300 bps since 2021 including 100 bps year to date. China is the exception, down about 130 bps over five years on disinflation.

Diesel and crude curves are in backwardation out to early 2028, which implies falling prices. Across energy and food, though, the whole futures curve has shifted up versus a few months ago, reflecting Strait of Hormuz disruption, the Russia-Ukraine war and the AI build.

Diesel is called an underestimated inflation driver. The diesel premium to crude hit $88 per barrel at the end of August versus a five-year average of about $31. Refined product flow through the strait is near 20% of capacity while crude flow is near pre-conflict levels.

Diesel supply is tight. US diesel exports are 27% above normal, US inventories are 14% below normal, Russia has restricted diesel exports, and Ukraine has hit Russian refineries. Even with the strait reopened, inventories would take time to rebuild and winter heating demand is coming.

On the Fed under Chair Kevin Warsh, the author calls the outlook highly uncertain because Warsh is curtailing information. His expectation is two to three more hikes before the Fed is done, and elsewhere one or two more hikes this year depending on jobs and wages.

Inflation expectations fell to 2.6% in early 2026, peaked at 6.6% within a few months of the US attack on Iran, and have returned to the mid-4% range. They remain well above the Fed's 2% target, including into 2027.

The MOVE Index (rate volatility) spiked in September, rivaling the spike after the US struck Iran. High-yield option-adjusted spreads rose less, so credit volatility is lower than pure rate volatility.
Year-to-date returns on Treasuries and IG corporates have turned negative. Bank loans, with floating rates, are up more than 3% year to date and outperforming the Agg by more than 600 bps.

Positioning advice: stay calm, keep bank loan and short-term allocations, and consider extending duration once the MOVE Index settles. IG corporate yields are in the 6% range and leveraged finance in the 8% range, which the author calls attractive.

sector_views.sector: Fixed income: bank loans and short-term investment grade
sector_views.rationale: Floating-rate bank loans benefit from rising rates and short-term IG has less duration exposure. Bank loans lead the Agg by more than 600 bps year to date.

sector_views.sector: Fixed income: long duration Treasuries and IG corporates
sector_views.rationale: Fixed-rate instruments fall when yields rise. The author suggests considering duration only after the MOVE Index settles.

earnings_insights: Nvidia increased its buyback authorization by $150B, a US record, bringing the total authorized amount to $235B. The report gives no earnings figures.
Meta's forecasted 2026 capital expenditures are $130B to $145B. The author says the Muse consumer AI agent launch helps justify the spending.

trade_ideas.description: Keep bank loan and short-term investment-grade allocations during rate volatility
trade_ideas.rationale: Floating-rate loans and short maturities hold up better when yields rise, and bank loans lead the Agg by more than 600 bps year to date.

trade_ideas.description: Extend duration in fixed income once the MOVE Index settles
trade_ideas.rationale: When rate volatility subsides the author sees a potentially attractive opportunity to extend duration.
trade_ideas.risk: Further Fed hikes and persistent inflation could keep yields rising.

risk_factors: Persistent high energy prices, especially diesel, feeding inflation.
Escalation or lack of resolution in the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption.
Russia-Ukraine war effects on refined product supply.
Further Fed rate hikes under Chair Warsh, who is curtailing information.
Inflation expectations remaining above the Fed's 2% target into 2027.
Heavy bond issuance tied to the AI infrastructure build.
Strained consumers with wage growth below inflation.
Credit spreads could widen if rate volatility transmits to corporate credit.
charts_described: Global Bond Selloff chart shows 10-year government yield changes in bps. 5-year changes: UK 438, US 372 (approximate reading), France 454 and Germany 367 range, Japan 298, China -131.
Atlanta Fed GDPNow chart for Q3 2026 shows a current estimate of 3.7%.
MOVE Index chart shows 150.27 on 9/30/2026 against the ICE BoFA High Yield OAS at 111.03 on 9/30/2026, indexed to October 2025 = 100.
Diesel premium to crude chart shows $88 in August 2026 versus a five-year average of $31.3 for the month.
Commodity curves chart shows WTI crude futures curve shifted upward from June 30 to September 30 readings, with diesel, corn and soy curves also shifted up.
vol_and_positioning: The MOVE Index spiked in September, rivaling the spike right after the US struck Iran. The chart shows it at about 111 on 9/30/2026 against a low near 76 in January and a peak near 156 in March, indexed to October 2025 = 100.
ICE BoFA High Yield OAS widened less than the MOVE Index in September but trended upward, so credit volatility is lower than rate volatility.
The author suggests a MOVE Index settling could signal a time to consider extending duration.
geopolitical: Conflict with Iran, including the US attack on Iran, with hopes for a resolution rising and then falling.
Disruption of seaborne traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, with refined product flows near 20% of capacity.
Russia-Ukraine war, including Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and Russian limits on diesel exports.
US midterm elections are weeks away.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI buildout is supporting growth. Without it the economy would likely be much slower and asset prices lower.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI build adds to inflationary pressure and bond issuance, and with high energy prices it strains the average worker. With stable energy, asset prices would be higher.

tension_points.bull_case: High-yield spreads have widened only modestly, so stress has not meaningfully reached corporate credit.
tension_points.bear_case: The MOVE Index spiked to levels rivaling the post-Iran-strike spike, signaling heightened macro uncertainty that could transmit to credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The MOVE Index settling would signal a time to consider extending duration.

theme_stances.key_argument: Diesel is an underestimated driver of inflation because almost everything is transported using it, and the premium to crude is nearly triple the norm.
theme_stances.evidence: diesel prices are an underestimated but fundamental driver of inflation in this cycle

theme_stances.key_argument: Bank loans adjust with rates and have outperformed the Agg by more than 600 bps year to date, so keep that allocation while volatility persists.
theme_stances.evidence: Keep a bank loan allocation and short-term allocation if you have them.

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation expectations remain above target and the author expects more hikes, though the path is highly uncertain.
